text:
mira: small follow-up from yesterday's format RFC. Hit a weird case where a quantized shard with an older header slipped through and caused NaNs in production GEMMs. Thinking we should add a tiny header-probe on open + optional background full-verify. quick convo?

jon: can you paste the minimal failure you saw?

mira: sure — repro log from the serving node:
```
[2026-04-02T14:23:07Z] load_shard ckpt-v12-part3.safetensors: index ok, header legacy
[2026-04-02T14:23:07Z] WARN loader: dtype mismatch expected=float16 found=quant8
[2026-04-02T14:23:07Z] RuntimeError: GEMM produced NaN at layer 34
```

sasha: rough. two UX models: 1) probe-on-open (fast header parse, fail early) or 2) lazy-verify (first-op check). Probe-on-open is nicer for users but costs a read/parse per shard.

dmitri: for Hosted/Dedicated I'm +1 probe-on-open. For Private we should expose a flag (probe_on_open=true/false). Default true for new uploads, false for legacy acceptance.

mira: my concrete API suggestion: WeightSource.open(path) still returns Reader + metadata map, but we add two optional string keys: `serializer_id` and `probe_status` with values: "unknown"|"header_ok"|"header_mismatch"|"deep_ok"|"deep_corrupt". No struct type changes. Backwards compatible.

jon: agreeable. How do we populate probe_status? header_ok if header fields parse and match expected serializer_id/schema_version. deep_* set by background verifier job.

sasha: what fields are we standardizing in the header? We should pick a compact, low-cost set: magic, serializer_id, schema_version, epoch, mini_sig (fast roll-up like blake2b-64), and optional full_checksum_url.

mira: suggested header example: magic="RSFT1", serializer_id="redwood.quant_v3", schema_version="1", epoch="2026-04-01-2", mini_sig="b2:9f3a7c" , full_checksum_url="s3://.../ckpt-v12.sha256"

dmitri: mini_sig must be fast to compute on readers (first N bytes or metadata-only). full checksum is authoritative.

ops: ops concern: failing shards at open could cause large numbers of model reload failures during rollout. We need a toggle + canary window and a dashboard showing `weights.open.failures` and `weights.deep_verify.flips`.

mira: rollout plan outline:
- Stage 1 (canary): enable header probe on 5% of traffic and emit metrics + logs. `probe_mode=sampled`
- Stage 2: enable for all new uploads; legacy checkpoints accepted but marked `probe_status=legacy` and queued for background verify when accessed
- Stage 3: after 30 days, optionally block legacy acceptance behind tenant-level policy (ops toggle)

jon: what should runtime do if probe_status==header_mismatch? Immediately try compatible fallback shard (float fallback or older-quant handler) and increment metric `weights.header_mismatch.count`. Also emit a span/event linking to checkpoint id.

sasha: Console: add a per-checkpoint "integrity" badge (green=deep_ok, amber=header_ok/legacy, red=deep_corrupt). For live flips to red, create alert + auto-ticket for Support for Dedicated/Private customers.

ci-bot: noted. I'll add a `serializer-roundtrip` integration to CI: write shard -> read with header probe -> compute full checksum -> ensure roundtrip status deep_ok. Hook on serializer repo PRs.

mira: implementation notes for eng-ml:
- loader: parse first X bytes to extract header only; avoid full deserialization on open
- WeightSource: metadata map keys `serializer_id` and `probe_status` (strings)
- verifier daemon: consumes access events, computes/requests full checksum, updates probe_status via metadata API
- runtime behaviour: on open header_mismatch -> try fallback variant, emit `weights.fallback.attempt` metric; if fallback fails move to error path and surface to customer

ops: telemetry: track `weights.open.latency` delta when probe-on-open enabled; track `weights.header_mismatch.rate` and `weights.deep_corrupt.count`. Add dashboard and canary alert thresholds.

dmitri: also add CI unit that simulates an old-serializer header and ensures probe rejects it (so we don't regress).

jon: small API compatibility note: callers that ignore metadata will be unaffected. For callers that relied on lazy NaN failures this will change failure timing but is better overall.

sasha: fine by me. I'll sketch Console mockups for the badge + incident flow.

mira: i'll open a tiny RFC patch with header schema, WeightSource metadata keys, verifier behaviour, runtime fallback + metrics, and rollout + ops toggles. Owners: mira (author), jon (loader), sasha (console), ops (rollout). Planning to land doc today and start a small PR early next week.

jon: SGTM

dmitri: SGTM

ops: SGTM — please coordinate canary windows with infra maintenance calendar

mira: thanks all, filing RFC now and tagging @team-eng-ml :eyes:
